nodes.name: NF Pretreatment
nodes.procedure: A piece of NF was initially pretreated through tip sonication for 5 min in a 1.5 M H2SO4 solution in DIW. The pretreated NF was thoroughly rinsed in DIW several times before further use.
nodes.source_text: a piece of NF was initially pretreated through tip sonication for 5 min in a 1.5 M H2SO4 solution in DIW. The pretreated NF was thoroughly rinsed in DIW several times

nodes.name: NiSx Interlayer Solvothermal Growth
nodes.procedure: 8 mmol of S8 powder was thoroughly dissolved in 70 mL of anhydrous toluene, followed by light stirring with two pieces (1.8×5 cm²) of pretreated NF. After 30 min of stirring, this was transferred to a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and solvothermal treatment was conducted for 6 h at 150°C. The resultant dark-gray NiSx@NF solids were thoroughly washed with DIW and air dried overnight.

nodes.name: Co-(NiFe)Ox Hydrothermal Deposition
nodes.procedure: Separately, 0.15 M Co(CH3CO2)2·4H2O, 0.23 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, and 0.08 M Fe(NO3)3·9H2O were dissolved in 64 mL of DIW under stirring. The two pieces of NiSx@NF from the previous step were added upon dissolution of metallic salts and light stirring was allowed for 5 min, followed by addition of 0.056 mol urea. 200 μL of NH4OH were added dropwise under light stirring, followed by 16 mL of DMSO. The 80 mL solution was transferred to a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and underwent hydrothermal treatment at 115°C for 6 h. The attained Co-(NiFe)Ox@NiSx@NF was rinsed with DIW and left to air-dry overnight.

nodes.name: Urea-assisted Nitridation
nodes.procedure: Chemical transformation of the top oxide layer to an oxynitride followed a urea-assisted nitridation method, whereby each 1.8×5 cm² Co-(NiFe)Ox@NiSx@NF sample was placed vertically standing in a downstream alumina crucible in a programmable tubular furnace. 4 g of urea in a different crucible was placed in the furnace upstream the sample, following Argon flow at a flowrate of 50 cm³ min⁻¹. This nitridation process was undertaken at 470°C for 2 h, with a heating rate of 15°C min⁻¹. The resultant Co-(NiFe)N@NiSx@NF was rinsed with DIW and left to air-dry overnight before any electrochemical testing was performed.

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM shows NiSx@NF with homogeneous surface distribution confirmed by elemental mapping, and Co-(NiFe)N@NiSx@NF displays larger surface area morphology than Co-(NiFe)N@NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The latter textural characterization technique was employed alongside elemental mapping on a freshly synthesized piece of NiSx@NF. As can be seen from Fig. 1a, the triangular shaped piece intentionally etched off the NiSx@NF prior to characterization shows a clear thickness difference along the NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals core-sheath structure with Ni3N (d=0.222 nm) and CoOOH (d=0.247 nm) phases; NiSx-interlayered sample shows more homogeneous elemental distribution and smaller quasi-amorphous surface thickness (~5-20 nm) vs phase separation in non-interlayered sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Bulk HRTEM imaging of the Co-(NiFe) based oxynitride samples was performed to determine the crystal structure... Lattice fringe determination on different regions of the samples strongly indicate a core-sheath like assembly.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms (Co,Ni)3S2 phases ((101), (110), (021), (104), (122) facets), Ni3N phase, CoN phases ((111), (311)), and α-CoOOH ((003), (017)) facets more prominent in NiSx-interlayered catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Higher resolution XRD data for 2θ between 18 and 46° and 52-88° are presented in Fig. 2g and 2h... Co(NiFe)N @ NiSx@NF exhibits several (Co,Ni)3S2 peaks corresponding to the (101), (110), (021), (104) and (122) facets.

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms yield BET surface areas of 44.7 m²/g for Co-(NiFe)N@Ni and 172.9 m²/g for Co-(NiFe)N@NiSx@Ni; BJH pore sizes 53.1 nm and 44.9 nm respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Specific surface areas of powder samples were obtained by applying the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) theory to N₂ adsorption-desorption isothermals... This is further showcased through BET analyses in Fig. S1a which resulted in calculated BET surface areas of 44.7 and 172.9 m²g⁻¹, and BJH average macropore sizes of 53.1 and 44.9 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio higher in NiSx-interlayered sample (Co 2p₃/₂ at 781.9/780.2 eV); confirms Co-N (778.2 eV), Ni-O-N (854.1 eV), Fe³⁺ (713.2 eV), M-O-N (533.1 eV), polysulfide to SO₃²⁻/SO₄²⁻ transformation post-OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 4a highlights the high-resolution Co 2p XPS spectra... Both as-prepared and post-OER Co 2p spectra for Co-(NiFe)N @ NiSx@NF exhibit a larger Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio relative to the Co-(NiFe)N @ NF sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: XAS shows lower Co oxidation state and higher Fe oxidation state in NiSx-interlayered samples; EXAFS confirms Co-O (1.56 Å), Co-N (1.47 Å), and metallic M-M coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We found that the as-prepared electrocatalysts exhibited a lower Co oxidation state for the NiSx interlayered sample... EXAFS analysis confirms the standard difference between both cobalt oxide and nitride characters present on the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman confirms Ni-S (Eg 250 cm⁻¹, E2g 306 cm⁻¹), Co-S modes, diminished Co3O4 (456 cm⁻¹) and NiO (543 cm⁻¹) peaks post-nitridation, cubic CoN (470 cm⁻¹).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Characteristic Ni-S bonds are confirmed in both the control NiSx@NF and Co-(NiFe)N @ NiS_x@NF samples, whereby both Ni-S (i.e., Eg (250 cm⁻¹) and E2g (306 cm⁻¹)) and Co-S vibration modes are clearly apparent.

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA of Co-(NiFe)N@NiSx@NF is 387.5 cm², over four times larger than non-interlayered counterpart.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Upon ECSA determination through the double-layer capacitance method... Co-(NiFe)N @ NiSx@NF exhibited 387.5 cm² of ECSA, which is over four times larger than that for the noninterlayered counterpart.
